issues.t: Rear frame rust can let the fuel tank drop (recall)
issues.sym: Heavy rust under the back of the truck, a fuel smell, a visible fuel leak, or a fuel tank that sags or hangs lower than normal.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, road salt and grime collect in the rear frame where the fuel tank straps mount. The steel can rust through until the tank is no longer held securely. Honda recalled 2006-2014 Ridgelines to inspect and repair the rear frame, and offers to buy back trucks that are too far gone.
issues.next: Run your VIN for open recalls and book the frame inspection. If you smell fuel or see the tank hanging low, do not drive it; have it towed.

issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger only shows up in a crash, when the driver air bag can deploy with too much force.
issues.why: The Takata driver air bag inflator uses a propellant that breaks down after years of heat and humidity. In a crash it can burst and throw metal pieces at the driver. Honda has recalled every model year of the first-generation Ridgeline, and some earlier replacement inflators were recalled again.
issues.next: Check your VIN now and get the inflator replaced for free. Older trucks that never had the repair are the highest risk, so do this right away.

issues.t: Passenger air bag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. In a collision, the front passenger air bag can burst and spray metal fragments.
issues.why: The passenger-side Takata inflator has the same propellant breakdown problem as the driver side. Several recalls cover 2006-2014 Ridgelines depending on year and the state where the truck was registered.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free replacement. Until it is done, avoid carrying a front passenger if you can.

issues.t: Radiator transmission cooler leaks and mixes coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Pink or milky fluid in the coolant tank, slipping or shuddering shifts, or a transmission that suddenly stops working right. Rusted fittings at the radiator may drip.
issues.why: The automatic transmission fluid is cooled by a small cooler built into the radiator. With age and corrosion, the cooler or its fittings can leak, so coolant and transmission fluid mix. Coolant in the transmission quickly ruins its clutches.
issues.next: If you see milky fluid or pink coolant, stop driving and have both fluids checked. Replacing an aging radiator before it fails is much cheaper than a transmission.

issues.t: Overdue timing belt or leaking tensioner can wreck the engine
issues.sym: Often no warning. Sometimes a slapping or ticking noise at the front of the engine, then the engine suddenly quits and will not restart.
issues.why: The 3.5L V6 uses a rubber timing belt and is an interference engine, so if the belt skips or breaks, the valves hit the pistons. A leaking hydraulic belt tensioner can let the belt go slack and jump teeth.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt, tensioner and water pump on schedule (around 100,000 miles, sooner if you tow). If the service history is unknown, do it now.

issues.t: Cylinder 4 misfire and oil burning
issues.sym: Check engine light with a cylinder 4 misfire code (P0304), rough running, and a puff of blue-gray smoke right after start-up.
issues.why: Owners of early Ridgelines report oil getting into cylinder 4 because of a broken or stuck piston ring, which fouls the spark plug and causes the misfire.
issues.next: First rule out a bad coil or plug by swapping them with another cylinder. If the misfire stays on cylinder 4 and oil is burning, get a compression or leak-down test before deciding on engine repair.

issues.t: Misfires on the rear cylinder bank
issues.sym: Check engine light, a flashing light under load, shaking at idle, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: The spark plugs on the rear bank sit under the cowl and are often left too long, and the ignition coils there run hot. A fouled plug or a failed coil causes the misfire.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Swapping the coil to another cylinder shows whether the coil or plug is at fault. Replace plugs in sets if they are due.

issues.t: Oil leak from the VTEC spool valve onto the alternator
issues.sym: Oil residue on the back of the engine, a burning oil smell, and eventually a battery or charging warning light when the alternator fails.
issues.why: The gasket under the VTEC spool valve on the rear of the engine hardens and leaks. The oil drips straight onto the alternator below it and ruins it.
issues.next: Have the spool valve gaskets replaced as soon as you see the leak. Catching it early saves the alternator.

issues.t: Rear differential groans or shudders in tight turns
issues.sym: A groan, moan, chatter or shudder from the back of the truck when turning slowly, such as in parking lots.
issues.why: The VTM-4 all-wheel-drive rear differential needs Honda VTM-4 fluid. When the fluid wears out or is contaminated with water, the clutches inside grab and chatter in turns. Using the VTM-4 lock button on dry pavement can also stress it.
issues.next: Have the rear differential fluid changed with the correct Honda fluid. Most trucks quiet down after one or two fluid changes.

issues.t: Power steering pump whines, mostly when cold
issues.sym: A whine or groan when turning the wheel, worst on cold mornings, sometimes with fluid seeping near the pump.
issues.why: A hardened O-ring on the pump feed pipe lets air into the system, and a clogged reservoir screen can starve the pump. The pump itself can wear out after that.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the feed-pipe O-ring and reservoir checked first; that cheap fix often stops the noise. Replace the pump only if the whine continues.

issues.t: Front-end clunk from sway bar links or ball joints
issues.sym: Rattling or clunking from the front over bumps, potholes or driveways.
issues.why: The front sway bar links wear out or break, and the lower control arm ball joints can wear on higher-mileage trucks.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn ball joints should be fixed promptly because they affect steering control.

issues.t: Gauge cluster display fails
issues.sym: The odometer or information display goes blank, flickers, or shows "not available".
issues.why: The gauge control module or its display fails. Honda issued service information on gauge module displays on early trucks.
issues.next: Have the cluster diagnosed. Rebuild services can repair the display for less than a new cluster.

issues.t: A/C or heater stops working
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or the fan and climate system will not come on at all.
issues.why: Common causes are a failed A/C compressor relay, a refrigerant leak, or a failed compressor. On some trucks the blower or climate control parts fail.
issues.next: Have the A/C relay checked first, since it is cheap. Fix leaks before recharging.

issues.t: Dual-action tailgate will not swing open
issues.sym: The tailgate folds down but will not swing open sideways, or it is hard to open in either mode.
issues.why: The tailgate latches, the actuator, or the rods connecting them fail or go out of adjustment. Honda has bulletins for early first-generation trucks and TSB 16-077 for the 2017 latch rod.
issues.next: Have the latches cleaned, lubed and adjusted. A failed latch or actuator may need to be replaced.

issues.t: Blower motor connector can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell from the passenger footwell, or the fan stops working.
issues.why: The blower wiring connector under the passenger side of the dash can be kicked loose and then overheat, with a risk of fire. Honda recalled these trucks to replace the connector and add a cover.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If you smell burning plastic, turn off the fan and get the truck checked.

issues.t: Fuel pump relay can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start because the fuel pump gets no power.
issues.why: A coil wire inside the fuel pump relay can break. Honda recalled the 2006 Ridgeline to replace the relay.
issues.next: Make sure the recall repair was done on your truck.

issues.t: Hood can fall shut when propped open (recall)
issues.sym: The hood drops suddenly while you are working under it.
issues.why: The hole for the hood support rod was not punched correctly on some trucks, so the rod can slip out. Honda recalled them to add reinforcement.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Until it is fixed, be careful working under an open hood.

issues.t: Fuel injector failure causes misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rough or shaking idle, misfires and loss of power.
issues.why: Fuel injectors on the direct-injection 3.5L V6 can fail early. Honda issued a service bulletin on injector-related misfires for its 3.5L V6 trucks and SUVs of this period.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and the injectors tested. If one injector has failed, many shops replace all six.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, will not start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank has a part that can swell and stick. Honda recalled 2017-2020 Ridgelines to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the pump replaced. If the engine starts running rough, have it looked at before it stalls in traffic.

issues.t: Fuel pump cover can crack from car wash soap (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or a fuel leak near the top of the fuel tank.
issues.why: Acidic cleaners, such as some car wash soaps, can crack the fuel pump feed port. Honda recalled these trucks to replace the pump if needed and add a protective cover.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and get the recall done.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing can wear and seize (recall)
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine, rough running, an oil pressure warning, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: A machining error on some crankshafts can wear out a connecting rod bearing until the engine seizes. Honda recalled some 2017 and 2019 Ridgelines; 2018 trucks were not in the recall population.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have it towed. The recall covers inspection and engine repair or replacement.

issues.t: Timing belt teeth can separate (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls suddenly and will not restart, sometimes with rattling first.
issues.why: Some timing belts were built with a defect that lets the teeth separate. Honda recalled these trucks to replace the belt and inspect the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN and make sure the belt was replaced.

issues.t: Rear subframe can rust at the suspension mounts (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, odd tire wear, the truck pulling or wandering, or visible rust and cracks near the rear suspension.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, the rear subframe can rust at the suspension mounts until it cracks, which can affect handling. Honda recalled these trucks to inspect and add a reinforcement kit.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the inspection, especially if you live where roads are salted.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor fault can affect the air bag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag status light shows the wrong setting, or the air bag warning light comes on.
issues.why: The weight sensor in the front passenger seat can crack and short out. Then the air bag may not turn off for a child or small adult, or could deploy when it should not. Honda has two recalls covering these trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Until the sensor is replaced, keep children in the back seat.

issues.t: Backup camera image goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen is black, flickers, or shows no image when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Opening and closing the tailgate flexes the camera wiring harness until the wires break. Honda recalled 2017-2019 and 2020-2025 Ridgelines to replace the harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Use your mirrors and look behind you until it is fixed.

issues.t: Hood can fly open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood is hard to latch, does not sit flush, or pops open at speed.
issues.why: The hood latch striker can be damaged, so the hood may not stay latched. Honda recalled these trucks to repair the striker or replace the hood.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If the hood ever fails to latch, do not drive until it is fixed.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can separate from the booster (recall)
issues.sym: A brake pedal that feels soft, travels farther or sinks, or less braking power than normal.
issues.why: A tie-rod fastener between the brake master cylinder and booster may have been assembled wrong at the factory, so the parts can separate. Honda recalled these trucks to inspect and repair them.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If the pedal feels different, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Steering gearbox ball joint can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock when turning, loose-feeling steering, or the truck pulling to one side.
issues.why: An inner ball joint housing in the steering gearbox may loosen and come apart, which can cause loss of steering control. Honda recalled 2023 Ridgelines to replace the gearbox if needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get it inspected right away.

issues.t: Air bag control unit may not deploy air bags (recall)
issues.sym: The air bag warning light may come on, but there may be no warning at all.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the air bag control unit could stop the air bags or seat belt pretensioners from working in a crash. Honda recalled some 2019 Ridgelines to replace the unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the control unit replaced.

issues.t: Engine may not restart after Auto Idle Stop
issues.sym: At a stop with Auto Idle Stop active, the engine shuts off as designed but then cranks and does not restart, or restarts very slowly.
issues.why: Honda found that excessive cylinder pressure and related factors could stop the engine from restarting. It issued software updates, valve adjustments and starter repairs through service bulletins (23-008, 23-009, 23-010) and extended warranty coverage. NHTSA opened an engineering analysis (EA25004) because complaints continued, and it lists the 2025 Ridgeline too.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the bulletins and the warranty extension apply to your VIN. Turning off Auto Idle Stop with the dash button avoids the problem until it is fixed.

issues.t: Collision braking system brakes for no reason
issues.sym: A sudden BRAKE warning or the truck braking hard when nothing is in the way, or collision warning errors on the dash.
issues.why: The Honda Sensing radar or camera can misread the road when it is out of aim, dirty or poorly calibrated.
issues.next: Keep the radar sensor in the grille and the camera area of the windshield clean. Report each event to a dealer and NHTSA, and ask for a sensor check and calibration.

issues.t: Transmission warning light or transmission failure
issues.sym: A "Transmission System Problem" message, harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, or a truck that will not move.
issues.why: Owners of 2017-2019 trucks with the 6-speed automatic report transmission faults and some complete failures.
issues.next: Have the codes read as soon as the warning appears. Ask the dealer about any software updates or warranty help.

issues.t: 9-speed automatic hesitates or shifts abruptly
issues.sym: A pause before the truck takes off, a bump or clunk when slowing down, or busy and abrupt shifts at low speed.
issues.why: The 9-speed automatic used from 2020 on is known for hesitant and abrupt low-speed shifts, often improved by software updates.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether a software update is available. If it gets worse, slips or shows a warning light, have it diagnosed.

issues.t: Oil leak on a new truck
issues.sym: Oil spots under the truck or oil on the engine within the first few hundred miles.
issues.why: An owner of a 2026 TrailSport reported an oil leak at about 150 miles, with a cracked cylinder head from the factory listed as the cause. It is an early single report, not a known widespread defect.
issues.next: Any oil leak on a new truck is a warranty repair. Take it to a Honda dealer right away and keep the paperwork.
